the hydrolysis rate of cellulose is increased by pretreatment with ionic liquids, that the rate of hydrolysis is increased by using a mixture of an ionic liquid with buffer, and that the stability and activity in an ionic liquids are enhanced by using a pure cellulose from Aspergillus.

the hydrolysis and pretreatment of cellulase using a pure cellulose: endo‐β‐1,4-glucanase (EC 3.2.1.4; EG) from the fungus Aspergillus Niger in buffer, the ionic liquid ( IL ) tris-(2-hydroxyethyl)-methylammonum methylsulfate, and various mixtures at various temperatures.
the hydrolysis and pretreatment of celluloses with the pure endoglucanse from A. niger and the ionic liquids HEMA and BMIM Cl, respectively.
the hydrolysis (degradation) of cellulose using an enzyme, endoglucanases (EG), in buffer and ionic liquid (BMIM Cl, HEMA, and BMIM Cl/HEMA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ionic liquid, HEMA, is a better solvent for cellulose than buffer, and that pretreatment of biomass with HEMA followed by hydrolysis with EG in a mixture of HEMA and buffer at high temperatures is more efficient for conversion of cellulose to glucose than hydrolysing untreated cellulose in buffer at low temperatures.
the ILs are able to increase the efficiency and yield of glucose from cellulose by pretreating it and also by acting as an efficient medium for hydrolyzing cellulose in the presence of EG.
the use of ionic liquids for cellulose hydrolytic reactions is a promising approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that cellulase is more active in ionic liquids than in water and that the pretreatment of cellulase with ionic liquids enhances the activity and stability of the enzyme.
we have shown that cellulases are more stable in ionic liquids (ILs) than in buffer.

the use of ionic liquids as a pretreatment for cellulose and subsequent hydrolysis of pretreated cellulose with a cellulase enzyme can be an attractive approach for bioconversion of cellulose to glucose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ionic liquids can provide an environment that enhances the stability and activity for cellulases, thereby improving the hydrolysis process.
the use of ILs as a solvent for cellulase can be a promising strategy to increase the efficiency and yield of cellulose hydrolyses.

the pretreatment of the cellulose with the IL, BMIM Cl, followed by hydrolysis in a 15% mixture of HEMA and buffer at 60°C, results in higher yields of glucose than the hydrolysis in pure buffer at 60 or 45°C.
